A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the controllability-based inference validation criterion is not equivalent to the network fidelity criterion.
, if one's goal is to use gene networks to design therapeutic interventions, then one should not be concerned with network fidelity as much as one should with controllability.

, if the purpose is to use a network for therapeutic interventions, then the network inference algorithm that best performs relative to controllabilty is not necessarily the best network inference algorithm relative to other measures of validity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, there is no one best inference procedure for all network models and applications.

, when one is using gene regulatory networks to develop intervention strategies, one should use a measure of validity that is based on the specific application at hand, rather than on network fidelity.
